Subject: Quick recap & next steps from today's discovery call

Hi Sahil —

Thanks for taking time today. Quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can validate budget ranges and procurement constraints: 

- Prod use case: customer support automation + NLU reranking for intent routing (mostly chat + async batch summarization).
- Expected monthly token profile you mentioned: 10–30M input tokens + ~20–60M output tokens (peak season) — could you confirm if that aligns with your internal projection?
- Target unit economics target you asked about: target $/1M tokens (net price) around $900–1,200? You mentioned procurement thresholds at $50k and $200k for different sign-off levels — can you confirm approvals required at those bands?

Next steps we propose:
1) You confirm the monthly spend band (best guess is $10k–$50k / $50k–$200k / $200k+ split).
2) We share a model of unit economics (gross cost, suggested volume discounts, recommended batching & caching assumptions) and a sample SOW for procurement.
3) If procurement prefers, we'll pull together the list of evidence (SOC2, data residency controls, KMS integration) to support the contract.

I've attached the RFP (you shared) and a short procurement checklist for reference.

Thanks — appreciate the openness here. If it's easier, happy to hop on a 20-min call with procurement next week.

Best,
Marissa

From: Sahil Mehta <sahil.mehta@zenpay.com>

Cc: Procurement <procurement@zenpay.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps from today's discovery call

Thanks Marissa — great summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token volumes: our product analytics team estimates steady-state 30–50M total tokens/month after Q3 ramp; worst-case peak 120–150M in heavy campaigns. The 10–30M estimate is on the low side for our roadmap.
- Budget bands & approvers:
  * <$50k/month: PM + Finance sign-off (fast)
  * $50k–$200k/month: Director level + Procurement review (2–3 week cycle)
  * >$200k/month: VP/CEO approval + legal redline (multi-month)

- Unit economics: procurement asked for net target pricing expressed as $/1M tokens. For internal targets they'd like to see three bands (pilot, steady-state, enterprise) and the assumptions that produce them (avg seq length, cache hit rates, batching).

We attached ProcurementThresholds.xlsx with the internal approval matrix. Procurement prefers we receive a clear uplift request (e.g., if final price > target) and an estimated time to production.

Can you send the example pricing model and a simple table mapping token ranges to monthly spend buckets for our review? Procurement wants the table surfaced in the SOW.

Cheers,
Sahil
Head of Product Ops | ZenPay
sahil.mehta@zenpay.com

Attachment: ProcurementThresholds.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sahil Mehta <sahil.mehta@zenpay.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap & next steps from today's discovery call

Appreciate the detail, Sahil — this is super helpful. Attached is a one-page model and a simple mapping table. High-level assumptions we used (we'll make these explicit in the SOW):

- Avg request: 40 tokens input, 120 tokens output (chat + summarization mix)
- Effective tokens per user: 160
- Cache/prefix hit: 18% (for FAQ/bot flows), batching efficiency: modest for low-latency routes

Proposed sample net pricing (illustrative) on Redwood Dedicated/Hosted:
- Pilot (0–30M tokens/month): $1,500 / 1M tokens (includes onboarding, basic support)
- Steady-state (30–150M tokens/month): $1,050 / 1M tokens (volume discounts applied)
- Enterprise (150M+ tokens/month): $800 / 1M tokens (custom SLA, reserved capacity)

Mapping table (tokens -> monthly spend):
- 0–30M -> $0.0k–$45.0k/month (pilot band)
- 30–150M -> $31.5k–$157.5k/month
- 150M+ -> $120k+ / month (enterprise pricing starts here)

Notes: pricing above is illustrative and assumes a 30% reduction in per-token compute cost once caching & batching are configured; exact net pricing will depend on contract term and commitment.

Next steps for us:
1) Rishi/Dylan: can you review the bands below and confirm we have flexibility on the enterprise threshold if procurement pushes?
2) Sahil: if this looks directionally correct, we can (a) include the table in an initial SOW and (b) schedule a procurement review session this week.

Thanks — attaching the pricing_model_v1.xlsx and short SOW stub.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Attachments: pricing_model_v1.xlsx, SOW_stub.docx
